_comment: The site's palette, in one place. Read by assets/css/global.scss (which has
front matter, so Jekyll runs it through Liquid before Sass sees it),
generators in bin/. Nothing else should hold a colour.
It lives in _data rather than _config.yml for three reasons: Jekyll loads
_data/*.json natively on the legacy GitHub Pages build with no plugin; Node
reads it with JSON.parse rather than the hand-rolled regex the generators
use for _config.yml, which only sees top-level scalars; and `jekyll serve`
watches data files, where a _config.yml edit needs a server restart.
Keys are underscored, not hyphenated: the site builds with Liquid's strict
error mode, and `colours.light.fg-strong` risks the hyphen being read as an
operator. The CSS custom property is still --c-fg-strong.
The pill is stored as a complete rgba() string rather than derived from the
background. Sass does not evaluate SassScript inside a custom property
value, so building it with a colour function there would emit invalid CSS
and fail silently. Keep it in step with `bg` by hand.
Contrast ratios against each theme's own ground are recorded beside the
tokens in assets/css/global.scss, where a reader of the theme will look.
